svg.title: Erdős #269 at the primes 2, 3, 5, set like a matrix. Left, the square of phases: down, the fractional part x of i log base 5 of 2 for a row; across, 1 minus the fractional part y of j log base 5 of 3 for a column. The diagonal x + y = 1 splits it: below, where the parts carry past 1, the rescaled kernel entry is 1/5 (red); above it is 1 (blue). Twelve rows and twelve columns, whose switch points alternate with the row phases, meet in 144 dots split by a staircase that crosses the diagonal at every one of them. Right, the selected minor: the same 144 entries evenly spaced, a staircase matrix with 1/5 on and below its diagonal. Each row differs from the row above only across one tread of the staircase, by -4/5, so its determinant is (1/5)(-4/5)^11.
